Tract II lies between the valleys of Tullock Creek and Sarpy Creek, and Tract III lies between the main valley of Sarpy Creek and the valley of the East Fork of Sarpy Creek. Total relief in the two tract areas is between 600 and 700 feet, ranging in altitude from a little more than 3,200 feet in the northern part of Tract III to nearly 3,900 feet in the southeast corner of Tract III. Local relief generally is not more than about 200 feet.
The floodplains of Tullock Creek and Sarpy Creek are nearly half a mile wide, but the valley floors of the tributary valleys, except for that of the East Fork of Sarpy Creek, generally are narrow and have little flat area. The valley walls commonly are steep (more than 20 degrees), with sandstone and clinker forming nearly vertical ledges and cliffs in some areas.
The upland areas of the lease tracts are dissected by tributary drainages that flow into Tullock and Sarpy Creeks. Where a coal bed has caught fire at the surface and burned, the overlying beds have been oxidized and partly fused to form a hard red rock called clinker.
